text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds pared gains in late trade after remaining moderately firm all day in a technical rebound from their sharp drop this week. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.79, down 0.22 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures suffered a bruising day after a surge in Britain's underlying average earnings and a sharp drop in unemployment claims caught the market by surprise. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-07/32, down 30/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures finished the MATIF session marginally weaker, with the June 10-year future failing to push through resistance at 128.16 during Wednesday's early gains and later ebbing with German and U.S. debt futures. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.90, down 0.02 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets ended firm but well within narrow range as players nervous about possibility of EMU delay and edgy over next direction of interest rates in U.S. Lira recovered some poise vs mark but still past 1,000 barrier. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.61, up 0.44 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened higher as investors anticipated a friendly February consumer price report. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-18/32, down 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.97 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed firmer after recouping earlier losses on the back of investors' consistent demand for cash bonds, scattered buying came in after midday with operators aiming to increase JGB holdings at their book closings. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.98, up 0.01 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A rash of retail-targeted offerings hit the primary market, leading the way was Caisse Centrale Desjardins du Quebec with a $250 million four-year deal priced to yield 32 basis points over the three-year U.S. Treasury note. There was an 18 b.p. difference between the three- and five-year U.S. Treasury notes at the time of pricing, a step-up of nine b.p. a year.
